metadata.title: To plan or not to plan: Technology integration in student teachers' lesson plans and their relation to dimensions of instructional quality

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study does not use an international large-scale assessment (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/ICILS) microdata file with sampling weights; instead, it analyzes anonymized written lesson plans produced by 130 German pre-service teachers during university seminars. The unit of analysis for the reported quantitative analyses is the 568 coded technology-integration instances extracted from those lesson plans, and the outcomes are ordinal/categorical codes derived from the SAMR model and instructional-quality coding scheme. Because the paper does not report any complex survey design, stratification, clustering, or application of sampling/replicate weights, no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) is available or applicable here. The main preparation steps are anonymization, instance identification, and systematic qualitative coding with reliability checks (Fleiss’ κ and Krippendorff’s α), rather than survey-weighted estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) are not applicable because the study does not use ILSA achievement scales (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/ICILS cognitive domains) that are typically PV-based; instead, it codes technology-integration levels (SAMR) and instructional-quality dimensions from written lesson plans. The outcomes are derived from qualitative coding into ordinal/categorical categories and then analyzed with non-parametric and logistic regression methods, not from PV-based test scores. Missing-data handling is not reported because the analysis is based on coded instances from lesson plans after anonymization and does not describe item-level missingness typical of survey/test datasets.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The corpus consists of lesson plans developed by 130 student teachers in German teacher education programs during undergraduate teacher-training seminars (2022–2024). Lesson plans were anonymized by removing/redacting identifying details before analysis. Technology-integration instances were identified in each lesson plan, yielding 568 coded instances (1–14 integrations per plan). Most lesson plans targeted grades 5–13, with 63% (n=82) for STEM subjects; age-related aspects were not coded. Coding reliability was established via trial coding by three coders on 10% (n=57) and an additional 10% (cumulative 20%) of instances (n=568), after which the remaining 80% (n=454) were coded by one coder using the finalized scheme.

main_findings.target_variable: predicting whether each instructional-quality dimension is addressed
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2023 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict predicting whether each instructional-quality dimension is addressed, finding that This paper is not an ILSA-based predictive ML study; it analyzes written lesson plans from 130 German pre-service teachers and codes 568 technology-integration instances using two frameworks: SAMR (substitution to redefinition) and three instructional-quality dimensions (cognitive activation, student support, classroom management). The study reports descriptive distributions and inferential associations using Spearman correlations, Kruskal–Wallis tests with Dunn–Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons, and binary logistic regression models predicting whether each instructional-quality dimension is addressed. Key results show that most integrations are at lower SAMR levels (substitution 61%, augmentation 27%), while cognitive activation is most frequent (28.7%), followed by student support (18.8%) and classroom management (17.6%). Associations are positive but modest: Spearman r values were 0.17 (cognitive activation), 0.37 (student support), and 0.10 (classroom management), and logistic regression McFadden pseudo-R² ranged from 0.02 to 0.14. Limitations include reliance on planned (not enacted) teaching and interpretive qualitative coding, with no survey-weighted estimation and no PV-based achievement outcomes. data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse for ML-specific fields because the article does not train or evaluate machine-learning models; it uses qualitative coding plus standard statistical tests (correlations, non-parametric group comparisons, and logistic regression) to examine relationships between coded categories. It also does not use ILSA cognitive achievement scores or PV-based outcomes, so PV handling and ILSA cycle/domain metadata are not applicable. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are left empty under the schema’s ML-focused requirements.
